title: How to Cut Pre-Bill Review Time With AI
summary: Pre-bill review time drops when entries arrive clean and AI takes the first markup pass. Which steps can AI remove?
body_markdown:
### AI Summary


-


Pre-bill review can take more than 10 hours per partner each month, much of it spent correcting time entries, checking billing guidelines, and managing repeated review rounds.


-


**Reduce pre-bill review time at the source** by using AI to generate complete, accurately assigned time entries before they reach the billing team.


-


Automate billing guideline checks and the first pre-bill markup pass so reviewers can focus on flagged exceptions rather than checking every entry manually.


-


Streamline the approval process with shared comments, automated routing, and fewer review rounds, while keeping partners responsible for commercial judgment and final approval.


-


**Measure time saved** by tracking partner review hours per billing cycle, review rounds per bill, and days from month-end to invoice delivery.


Pre-bill review commonly consumes[10+ hours per partner per month](https://pointone.com/blog/optimizing-legal-pre-bill-proforma-review) . The commercial cost of slow[pre-bill review](https://pointone.com/blog/law-firm-pre-bill-review) extends beyond the hours spent reading bills. Every incomplete entry, missed rule, and recirculated edit adds administrative work before the firm can invoice. Reducing pre-bill review time therefore starts with where that work can be prevented, not with how reviewers can move through it faster.

## Step 1: Fix Entries Before They Reach the Pre-Bill


Review time is set at the moment of entry. A vague or late entry costs a reviewer more time than a complete entry costs the timekeeper to make.


Set operating parameters before changing the technology. Entries should be released daily or weekly rather than held until month-end. The billing admin should own the chase, and a fixed cutoff date should close the entry window before the pre-bill run.


[AI time capture](https://pointone.com/blog/ai-time-capture) observes the work itself and classifies each activity to the correct client and matter, generating a draft from that activity. The narrative and matter arrive with the entry instead of being reconstructed later from memory.


That moves corrective work out of pre-bill review. The first reviewer receives an entry that can be checked rather than a gap that must be investigated.


## Step 2: Turn Billing Guidelines Into Rules Checked at Entry


A guideline checked at entry never becomes a pre-bill markup.


[Outside Counsel Guidelines](https://pointone.com/blog/outside-counsel-guidelines) can govern staffing, narrative requirements,[task codes](https://pointone.com/blog/the-ultimate-guide-to-utbms-codes) , block billing, rates and invoice timing. Matter-specific terms can also include a staffing plan, budget, billing increment or exception to the client's standard requirements.


The checks that one entry can answer on its own should move upstream. A missing code, prohibited term, wrong increment, vague narrative or likely block billing can be identified when the entry is created. Duplicate work, inconsistent times recorded across timekeepers for the same event, cumulative caps and discounts still require a pre-bill view because they depend on more than one entry.


This division makes[OCG compliance](https://pointone.com/blog/ocg-compliance-process) manageable. One owner should maintain the firm's guideline library. The terms of a new engagement should be entered before the first time entry is written against it.


A rule found after the bill goes out creates rework. If the affected time is written off, that rework also reduces the firm's[realization rate](https://pointone.com/blog/blog-law-firm-realization-rate) .


## Step 3: Let AI Take the First Markup Pass


The first markup pass is pattern work rather than judgment work.


That pass can identify vague narratives, block billing, duplicate work, inconsistent time recorded by different timekeepers for the same call where the client's guidelines require it, and entries assigned to the wrong matter. A reviewer still accepts or rejects every suggested edit, and nothing is billed without a person confirming it.


[PointOne Review](https://pointone.com/product/review) marks up pre-bills, flags problems and suggests fixes.[PointOne Rules](https://pointone.com/product/rules) turns uploaded guidelines into structured billing rules, then checks every time entry and pre-bill against them.


Together, these functions allow the first reviewer to work from exceptions rather than search every line for familiar problems. The partner receives a cleaner bill with unresolved items made visible.


## Step 4: Replace Recirculation With One Shared Review


The hours lost between review rounds come from edits that travel as comments and return as new versions of the bill.


In the same review tool, comments remain attached to entries instead of moving through separate email threads. Set up routing once, and each pre-bill moves through its reviewers in order, such as legal assistant, responsible partner and billing admin. The bill’s action log records every change and allows reviewers to restore the bill to any previous point.


The operating parameters are simple: define one routing order for each client and assign a deadline to every step. A shared record reduces version reconciliation and makes it clear who has the next decision.


## Step 5: Keep the Partner on the Judgment Calls


AI cuts the partner's time by removing clean-up work, not by taking the decisions.


The responsible partner should retain the reasonableness call on the time spent and any write-offs or agreed discounts. The partner also judges how the bill will read to that particular client. These decisions depend on the matter, the relationship and the commercial context.


The partner should see flagged items that require judgment and then give final sign-off. That removes the need to reread every line for routine defects that could have been caught earlier.


## How Should a Firm Measure the Time It Saves?


Measure three numbers before and after the change rather than treating review as one undifferentiated process.


1.


**Partner review hours per billing cycle.** Record the time partners spend reviewing and approving bills.


2.


**Review rounds per bill.** Count how often a bill moves between reviewers before approval.


3.


**Days from month close to invoice sent.** Track whether fewer corrections and handoffs shorten the path to invoicing.


Write-downs caught during pre-bill review versus after the client sees the bill are a useful fourth measure. A firm should establish its own baseline during the first cycle rather than adopt a general benchmark.

## FAQs about Pre-Bill Review Time


How Long Should Pre-Bill Review Take?


The answer depends on matter volume, guideline load and the number of review steps. A firm should measure its own partner hours, review rounds and invoice timing before setting an internal benchmark.


Can AI Approve a Pre-Bill on Its Own?


No. AI can flag problems and suggest edits, but a reviewer accepts or rejects each proposed change, and nothing is billed without human confirmation.


Does AI Pre-Bill Review Replace the Billing Team?


AI pre-bill review moves the billing team away from repetitive line edits and toward exceptions, routing and unresolved requirements. The team still manages the process and handles issues that require context or coordination.


What Is the Fastest Change a Firm Can Make?


Shorten the gap between the work and the entry. Frequent entry release gives reviewers better information and reduces the reconstruction required at month-end.
